If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+y)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{sin}⁡y).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{sin}⁡y), & 0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-\frac{\pi }{6}<Y\le \frac{\pi }{12}) & ={\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /12}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /12}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)+\operatorname{cos}⁡y]}_{0}^{\pi /12} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}[(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{12})+\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{12})-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡0)] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{2}}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-1) \\  & ≈0.4177.\end{aligned}
$$
